content:
Ava (support): FYI a large customer reported that after our last model push the /rerank endpoint is returning wildly different scores for the same queries. They say nothing else changed on their side.
Sam (support): Ugh. Can you paste a minimal repro (input + scores) and the model name they hit?
Ava (support): Pasted below from the customer (anonymized). They call rerank with model=redwood-rerank-2026-02 and see different scores between yesterday and today for identical inputs.
Ava (support): ```json
POST /v1/rerank
Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxxx
{
  "model": "redwood-rerank-2026-02",
  "queries": ["how to reset api key"],
  "candidates": ["reset in console > security > keys","contact support to reset","rotate via api" ]
}
----
response A (yesterday): [0.78, 0.12, 0.10]
response B (today):     [0.46, 0.38, 0.16]
```
Sam (support): Thanks. Did they include any headers, custom params (seed, temperature), or a batching wrapper?
Ava (support): No, plain SDK call from their backend. They said they didn't change code.
Rafael (ml-eng): Likely culprits: a model variant swap, tokenizer merge changes, or an update to the reranker scoring head (loss->logit normalization). Also quantization/compilation could change numeric ordering. We need to check exact model artifact hashes between yesterday and today. @Priya can you pull deployment metadata for redwood-rerank-2026-02?
Priya (eng): On it. I see a deployment event yesterday at 2026-03-11T18:02Z and a canary rollout to ~10% traffic at 2026-03-12T02:15Z. deploy-bot: "canary deployed redwood-rerank-2026-02 -> tag: v2.3.0-beta (10% traffic)"
deploy-bot: "full rollout scheduled: manual approval required"
Jules (ml): If the canary changed tokenization (e.g., new merges) or we changed the canonical input preprocessor (strip/normalize whitespace), scores for short strings can flip. Another possibility: we started applying per-candidate length normalization accidentally.
Rafael (ml-eng): Agreed. Also check whether the server-side reranker started using softmax temperature or changed score scaling (logit vs prob). That would change absolute numbers but not necessarily ranking — here ranking changed (candidate 1 dropped to second).
Sam (support): Customer says ranking order changed which broke their business rule. They're upset. We need a repro we can run ourselves and a rollback plan.
Ava (support): Repro steps I ran locally (mac) — I set up a curl call and got the same drift as the customer. Repro snippet: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_KEY" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-rerank-2026-02","queries":["how to reset api key"],"candidates":["reset in console > security > keys","contact support to reset","rotate via api"]}'
```
Ava (support): Output I saw (prod): [0.78,0.12,0.10] vs (canary): [0.47,0.37,0.16].
Priya (eng): I collected model hashes. Prod currently points at artifact sha: sha256:aa11... and canary points at sha256:bb22... They are different builds of the same model name. I'll diff the model config files (tokenizer.json, model_config.json, scoring_config.json).
Jules (ml): Please also dump token ids for the query + candidates on both builds. Differences there would indicate tokenizer change. Example: ```python
from redwood_tokenizer import Tokenizer
Tk = Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json')
print(Tk.encode('how to reset api key'))
```
Rafael (ml-eng): I'll run a deterministic scoring job: ensure temperature=0, top_k=1, seed=0, disable TPU/quantization flags so we compare fp32 logits. If the logits differ signficantly after that, it's a model/artifact issue not sampling nondeterminism.
Sam (support): Customer asks ETA on rollback — we should treat this high priority. Any risk to other customers if we roll back? Priya?
Priya (eng): The canary was only 10% and hasn't been promoted. I can roll back the canary to the previous artifact within 30 minutes, but need approval from product. Rolling back will revert the new artifact everywhere the canary ran; logging/metrics will be preserved.
Ava (support): @product please advise — customer impacted is on a paid plan and will escalate to their CTO soon.
Jules (ml): Quick debug results from my side: token ids changed. Example tokenization diff:
- prod ids: [45, 12, 300, 16, 98]
- canary ids:[45, 12, 305, 16, 98]  # 'api' merges to different id due to new merges.
Jules (ml): That shift alone can change embedding/feature inputs and thus scores. It's consistent with the observed behaviour.
Rafael (ml-eng): That makes sense. Two action items: 1) rollback canary to restore stable behavior; 2) add regression test that runs selected customer queries through tokenizer + scoring before promoting artifacts.
Priya (eng): Rolling back now. deploy-bot: "rollback initiated for redwood-rerank-2026-02 canary -> restoring sha256:aa11..."
deploy-bot: "rollback complete: canary back to sha256:aa11... (10% traffic)"
Ava (support): I re-ran the curl test after rollback — scores now match prod original [0.78, 0.12, 0.10]. Customer notified and asked for root cause update.
Sam (support): I created internal ticket CS-672 (severity P1) and attached tokenizer diffs, model hashes, and the customer's repro. Assigned to @Jules and @Priya for RCA and regression tests.
Jules (ml): RCA summary draft: tokenizer merges changed in builder pipeline (automated vocab update pulled from external merges repo). This changed token IDs for short functional tokens ('api') causing embedding differences that cascaded to rerank scores. We will pin tokenizer digest for reranker models and add a pre-deployment check that compares a small set of canonical queries.
Priya (eng): I'll implement the pre-deploy hook in the CDN/orchestration pipeline: when a model artifact is staged, run the canonical rerank eval with baseline tolerance thresholds (both ranking and score deltas). Block promotion if drift > threshold.
Rafael (ml-eng): Also propose we store and surface tokenizer version in console and API: model.tokenizer_id so customers can pin or be aware.
Ava (support): Customer requested a writeup and ETA for permanent fix. I'll share RCA + timeline. ETA for fixes?
Priya (eng): I'll have a PR for the pre-deploy check by EOD tomorrow and a deployment to dev by end of week.
Jules (ml): I'll add the canonical queries and the tokenizer pinning proposal to CS-672.
Sam (support): Thanks team. Follow-ups: 1) notify impacted customers who hit rerank, 2) update changelog noting tokenizer pinned for rerank models, 3) draft support-facing KB article explaining why tokenizers can affect scores and what customers can do (pin models or supply tokenized candidates).
Ava (support): I'll notify the account team and draft the KB.
Priya (eng): Marking CS-672 with labels: regression, tokenizer, blocker.
Rafael (ml-eng): One more note for long-term: add unit tests that confirm stable candidate ordering for canonical queries across tokenizer updates (or produce an explicit warning when tokenizer changes).
Ava (support): Customer confirmed they're unstuck for now after rollback, but want follow-up when fixes are in place. I'll keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
Sam (support): Closing loop here but keeping ticket open until RCA + tests merged.
